questions.q: What is a data connector in Sentinel?
options: A physical network cable used only for on-prem SIEM hardware
A feature that deletes old data from the workspace automatically
A pre-built integration that pulls logs from a source and writes them into one or more workspace tables
A type of KQL query used for hunting
questions.explain: A data connector is what actually brings logs from a source into the Log Analytics workspace tables Sentinel reads from.

questions.q: What distinguishes a service-to-service connector, such as the Microsoft Entra ID connector?
options: It's a cloud-to-cloud integration that requires no installed agent, close to a single toggle to enable
It requires installing software on every machine in the environment
It cannot bring in sign-in or audit log data of any kind
It only works for on-premises Linux servers
questions.explain: Service-to-service connectors like Entra ID or Office 365 pull directly from another Microsoft service's API with nothing to install.

questions.q: Why does collecting Syslog/CEF data from a third-party firewall typically require an agent-based connector?
options: Because agent-based connectors are only used for Microsoft Entra ID
Because firewalls cannot generate any log data at all
Because Syslog and CEF are exclusive to AWS CloudTrail
Because the firewall isn't a native Microsoft cloud service, so the Azure Monitor Agent is used to forward its logs to the workspace
questions.explain: Agent-based connectors use the Azure Monitor Agent, installed on a machine, to forward logs like Syslog/CEF from non-cloud-native sources.

questions.q: How does Sentinel typically bring in AWS CloudTrail logs?
options: Only by manually copying log files between accounts
AWS CloudTrail cannot be connected to Sentinel under any circumstances
By installing the Azure Monitor Agent directly inside AWS CloudTrail
Through an API-based connector that authenticates into AWS via a cross-account role and reads from an S3 bucket
questions.explain: The AWS connector is API-based: it uses a cross-account role and an S3 bucket where CloudTrail deposits logs, not an installed agent.

questions.q: What should you check first if a detection rule seems to be missing expected data?
options: Nothing — connector status has no bearing on rule results
Whether the rule's KQL syntax uses semicolons
Whether the Sentinel license has expired, which is the only possible cause
Whether the relevant data connector shows a status of 'Connected' and is landing data in the expected table
questions.explain: A connector not showing Connected means no data is reaching its table, which is the first thing to rule out before blaming the rule's logic.
